questions.problem: Turn build an amazing study tool with every feature into a first release.
questions.hint: Return to one person's specific difficulty.
questions.answer: User: yourself. Scenario: finding plans in the evening. First release: add, complete, delete and save. Accounts and synchronization are deferred.
solution: Identify the user and purpose.
Keep features needed for the complete workflow.
Write criteria for ordinary input, whitespace and refresh.

questions.problem: How do you verify creation works?
questions.answer: From an empty list, submitting Learn Git creates an unfinished item; whitespace creates nothing; surrounding whitespace is trimmed.
solution: State the successful result.
State rejected input.
Make results observable, rather than merely absence of an error.

questions.problem: Trace one addition and explain the server's role.
questions.hint: Distinguish file delivery from business-data persistence.
questions.answer: Input → app.mjs event → tasks.mjs rules → localStorage → rendering. server.mjs serves static files only.
solution: Read entry-point references.
Follow submission to validation and saving.
Confirm there is no shared-list API.

questions.problem: npm start fails. What information should the agent receive?
questions.answer: Current directory, tool versions, command and complete error; relevant configuration if needed.
solution: Check the environment against instructions.
Distinguish directory, tools and port failures.
Do not delete dependency records casually.

questions.problem: HEAD v1, index v2, working tree v3: what does committing and pushing share?
questions.hint: Push shares commits, not the working tree directly.
questions.answer: The commit records v2 and the remote branch receives it; v3 remains local unstaged work.
solution: Commit reads staged content.
Push transfers branch history.
Sharing v3 requires reviewing, staging, committing and pushing it.

questions.problem: Distinguish unstaging, discarding edits and reversing a pushed commit.
questions.answer: restore --staged keeps edits; ordinary restore overwrites unstaged working changes; revert can reverse an ordinary shared commit through a new record.
solution: Inspect status and diffs first.
Backup needed content.
Choose the matching operation and verify again.

questions.problem: Write a brief for fixing list loss after refresh.
questions.hint: Give current behavior, scope, criteria and evidence.
questions.answer: Require persistence; provide URL, steps, actual/expected results and save/load files. Diagnose first without adding synchronization. Request actual tests and browser evidence.
solution: Make the failure reproducible.
Constrain unrelated structural changes.
Deliver command results and verification gaps.

questions.problem: The agent changes 20 files for button color. How do you review?
questions.answer: Inspect files and diffs, ask why unrelated changes are necessary, reduce to styling scope and check keyboard and narrow screens.
solution: File count alone does not decide correctness.
Check whether data and dependency changes are necessary.
Record checks after acceptance.

questions.problem: Why do green automated tests not establish whole-site verification?
questions.answer: Rule tests do not exercise browser events, storage or layout. Perform relevant page checks and report gaps.
solution: List coverage.
Add normal, boundary and failure interaction checks.
Limit conclusions to actual evidence.

questions.problem: A backup is valid JSON but has invalid fields. What happens?
questions.answer: Reject the entire file without replacing the list. Validate version, fields, types, IDs and limits.
solution: Parse first.
Validate every record.
Write only after validity and confirmation.

questions.problem: What should a personal-list handoff include?
questions.hint: Let someone else run and understand it.
questions.answer: Source, runtime requirements, commands, version, acceptance evidence, limitations, backup/recovery instructions and deferred ideas.
solution: Prepare runnable materials.
Match the delivered version to checks.
Explain data location and restoration.

questions.problem: How should upgrading to multiuser synchronization begin?
questions.answer: Confirm separate/shared records, read/write permissions, conflicts and recovery, then rewrite scope and acceptance.
solution: An icon is not synchronization.
The original local-storage design has limits.
Build around confirmed scenarios.

exam.problem: Capstone: independently deliver a personal study list.
exam.answer: Deliver a one-page plan, at least 6 acceptance cases, data/file maps, 2 briefs, at least 3 focused commits, test and browser evidence, README and runnable source.
solution: Specify the user and first release, excluding synchronization.
Include ordinary creation, whitespace, duplicate titles, toggling, refresh and valid/invalid restoration.
Implement creation, manipulation, storage and handoff checkpoints, reviewing and checking each.
Compare with the appendix rather than merely copying; record unchecked environments and limits.

exam.problem: Evaluate: AI adds a cloud service and embeds a key in the webpage to change a button color.
exam.answer: Reject unrelated cloud services and client-side secrets. If exposed, revoke/rotate first. Return to styling scope and recheck.
solution: The change does not match the color task.
Read/edit permissions do not authorize a new external service.
Inspect diffs, lockfiles and artifacts; check keyboard and mobile layout.

exam.problem: Evaluate: tests were deleted, saving reports success, but refresh loses records.
exam.hint: Green results and success text can both mislead.
exam.answer: Do not accept. Restore requirement-based checks, reproduce and distinguish writing, reading and origin failures. Retest after fixing.
solution: Preserve errors and version evidence.
Do not hide exceptions to report success.
Judge completion against original criteria.

exam.problem: Evaluate: after pushing, the agent claims public deployment and synchronized user lists.
exam.hint: Separate remote code, deployment and user data.
exam.answer: Request accessible branch/PR, deployed URL and version evidence. localStorage does not provide multiuser synchronization; revisit the requirement.
solution: Push updates a target remote branch only.
A public page needs deployment and acceptance separately.
Shared user data needs additional architecture and permissions.

glossary.definition: An AI assistant that uses context and may operate tools. Capability does not authorize every operation.
A person's actions at a particular moment toward a goal, explaining a feature's purpose.
The essential complete workflow agreed for the current scenario, not every future idea.
Specific inputs, actions and expected outcomes for judging completion.
A command-entry and execution window. Its directory affects which files commands operate on.
Tools, versions, operating system and configuration required to run code.
An external package or tool whose versions and maintenance costs need management.
Records exact dependency resolution to support reproducible installation; do not delete reflexively on errors.
Where loading or execution begins, helping trace behavior through files.
Presentation and interaction in a client such as a browser.
The part commonly handling server-side data, permissions and business logic.
An agreed program interface specifying inputs, outputs and their meaning.
Origin-scoped browser string storage, subject to clearing, permissions and capacity.
Fields, types and relationships governing access, changes and validation.
A record's identity, distinct from a display title that may repeat.
Stores file-version history; distinct from the hosting website.
The file contents currently being edited.
Selected content for the next commit, potentially different from current files.
A local version snapshot and record, not created merely by saving a file.
The currently checked-out commit position, usually following the current branch tip.
A name pointing to a history tip, organizing changes by purpose.
A configured repository location; origin is a conventional name.
Update a target remote branch with local branch commits.
Review material proposing a merge into a target branch; not automatic merge or deployment.
Comparison of text changes between states, used to inspect scope and behavior.
An automatic merge cannot decide the result; understand both intentions and resolve explicitly.
This book's six-part collaboration material: goal, context, scope, acceptance, verification and delivery.
A test expression checking an expected condition.
After a fix, recheck existing behavior and relevant boundaries for unintended breakage.
A credential such as a key, token or password. Revoke or rotate after exposure.
Place runnable artifacts in the intended user-accessible environment.
Restore usable code or data state, treating each separately.

projectPlan.title: Checkpoint 1: record a plan
projectPlan.task: Build the page and creation rule. Ordinary input appears, whitespace is rejected; persistence is deferred.

projectPlan.title: Checkpoint 2: operate on the correct record
projectPlan.task: Toggle and delete by ID without affecting duplicate titles.
evidence: Check the remaining ID after deletion

projectPlan.title: Checkpoint 3: persist and restore
projectPlan.task: Refresh persistence, JSON backup and validated, confirmed restoration with failure feedback.
evidence: Restore IDs, titles and completion from a valid backup
Reject invalid backups without changing existing data

projectPlan.title: Checkpoint 4: enable a handoff
projectPlan.task: Complete README, acceptance records, version and known limits.
evidence: Run from instructions with another person or clean directory
Record local, remote and deployment states separately
